components.name: First-aid Row
components.description: Row of four symptom-first links between hairlines on the home page.
components.html: טבלת תסמיניםOne-line descriptionאיפה זה רץOne-line description
components.css: .ds-firstaid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(11.5rem, 1fr)); border-block: 1px solid #26322c; direction: rtl; font-family: Heebo, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-firstaid a { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.15rem; padding: 0.8rem 0.9rem; text-decoration: none; color: #f2f7f4; border-inline-end: 1px solid #26322c; transition: background-color 160ms ease-out; } .ds-firstaid a:last-child { border-inline-end: 0; } .ds-firstaid a:hover { background: #123029; } .ds-firstaid a:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #41c4aa; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-firstaid b { font-family: Rubik, Heebo, sans-serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: 1rem; color: #41c4aa; } .ds-firstaid span { font-size: 0.875rem; color: #8fa198; line-height: 1.45; }

narrative.overview:
This is a technical reference set the way a printed manual is set: reading text on a quiet ground, structure carried by type weight and hairline rules, one teal accent reserved for links and current state. It serves one student mid-exam on a second monitor, scanning for a command, copying it and going back to the terminal. Nothing decorative stands between the eye and the term it wants. Starlight's chrome stays; the build re-skins it with the guide-family world: green-tinted neutrals (hue about 150) in place of Starlight's blue-gray.

Density is operational but not cramped: 17px body at 1.7 line height, tables at 15px, headings on a tight fixed rem scale. Dark is the default theme and light is a full peer. Hebrew prose runs RTL; every command, flag and technical term is English and stays LTR and unbroken.
keyCharacteristics: Hairlines (1px) and a heavier 2px rule divide content; boxes are rare and tinted, never shadowed.
One accent hue (teal), used for links, current state, focus and the runs-on pill only.
Heebo for reading, Rubik for headings and labels, JetBrains Mono strictly for code.
Amber is reserved for placeholders; callout hues carry fixed meaning.
Flat: no shadows anywhere in the build.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Teal marks navigation and state only. It never fills a large area and never decorates.

rules.name: The Amber Is Placeholder Rule
rules.body: Amber on a code token means "replace me". Trap callouts use a related warm hue, but as a quiet field, never as the saturated chip.

rules.name: The Paired Theme Rule
rules.body: Any new color is defined for dark and light together as a custom property; no theme-specific one-offs in component rules.

rules.name: The Mono Is Literal Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono appears only for code, commands, paths, keycaps and "runs on" labels. Never for emphasis or decoration.

rules.name: The Never-Split Rule
rules.body: Inline code is nowrap with ligatures off, so a flag like --force is never broken at its hyphen and copies exactly. Markdown smartypants is off for the same reason.

rules.name: The Hairline Over Box Rule
rules.body: Separate with a rule or a whitespace gap before reaching for a bordered box. Where a field is needed, it is tinted with a 1px rule in a matching hue.

dos: Do keep Hebrew prose RTL and all code, commands, flags and technical terms English and LTR.
Do use teal only for links, current state and focus (2px focus ring, 2px offset, in the theme's accent).
Do define any new color as a dark and light custom-property pair.
Do keep callout meanings fixed: note = intro, caution = trap, danger = destructive, tip = principle.
Do give every command block a title that says where it runs.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion; the only transition in the build is a 160ms background fade on first-aid links.
donts: Don't use amber for anything except placeholders and trap callouts' quiet field.
Don't set Hebrew text in mono or put code inside an RTL flow without isolation.
Don't add shadows, thick side-stripe borders or boxed card grids; the house voice is hairlines and tinted fields.
Don't let smartypants or ligatures alter a command; commands must copy exactly.
Don't open the home page with a hero or same-size icon cards; it is an index.
